- main:
  - heading "You said:" [level=4]
  - generic: Which privacy-friendly website analytics tools should a small SaaS business shortlist as alternatives to Google Analytics? Recommend up to five brands, explain the tradeoffs briefly, and cite sources if available.
  - group "Your message actions":
    - button "Copy message":
  - heading "ChatGPT said:" [level=4]
  - paragraph:
    - text: For a small SaaS, I’d shortlist these five. The key tradeoff is
    - strong: privacy/simplicity vs. depth of user-level product analytics
    - text: —none is a perfect 1:1 replacement for everything GA4 can do.
  - table:
    - rowgroup:
      - row "Tool Best for Main tradeoff":
        - columnheader "Tool"
        - columnheader "Best for"
        - columnheader "Main tradeoff"
    - rowgroup:
      - row "Plausible Best overall GA replacement Very simple and privacy-friendly, but intentionally lacks GA4-style user-level analysis":
        - cell "Plausible":
          - strong:
            - link "Plausible":
              - /url: https://plausible.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
              - text: Plausible
        - cell "Best overall GA replacement"
        - cell "Very simple and privacy-friendly, but intentionally lacks GA4-style user-level analysis"
      - row "Fathom Analytics Polished, low-maintenance analytics Excellent simplicity/privacy, but less customizable than heavier analytics platforms":
        - cell "Fathom Analytics":
          - strong:
            - link "Fathom Analytics":
              - /url: https://usefathom.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
              - text: Fathom Analytics
        - cell "Polished, low-maintenance analytics"
        - cell "Excellent simplicity/privacy, but less customizable than heavier analytics platforms"
      - row "Umami Technical teams wanting control Open source and self-hostable, but self-hosting means you own the infrastructure/maintenance":
        - cell "Umami":
          - strong:
            - link "Umami":
              - /url: https://umami.is/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
              - text: Umami
        - cell "Technical teams wanting control"
        - cell "Open source and self-hostable, but self-hosting means you own the infrastructure/maintenance"
      - row "Matomo Closest privacy-conscious alternative to GA4 Much deeper feature set, but consequently more complex; some configurations use cookies/require consent":
        - cell "Matomo":
          - strong:
            - link "Matomo":
              - /url: https://matomo.org/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
              - text: Matomo
        - cell "Closest privacy-conscious alternative to GA4"
        - cell "Much deeper feature set, but consequently more complex; some configurations use cookies/require consent"
      - row "Simple Analytics Maximum simplicity/privacy Aggregate traffic analytics rather than detailed individual-user journeys":
        - cell "Simple Analytics":
          - strong:
            - link "Simple Analytics":
              - /url: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
              - text: Simple Analytics
        - cell "Maximum simplicity/privacy"
        - cell "Aggregate traffic analytics rather than detailed individual-user journeys"
  - button "Copy table":
  - heading "My take" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - strong: 1. Plausible — best default for most small SaaS businesses.
    - text: Plausible is open source, EU-based, cookieless, and says it collects no personal data and doesn't sell visitor information. Its interface and implementation are deliberately lightweight.
    - link "Plausible Analytics +2 Plausible Analytics +2":
      - /url: https://plausible.io/privacy?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Plausible Analytics
      - generic: "+2"
      - generic: Plausible Analytics
      - generic: "+2"
    - strong: "Choose it if:"
    - text: you primarily need traffic, acquisition channels, pages, goals/events, and a clean dashboard.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: 2. Fathom — best polished hosted option.
    - text: I'd put Fathom alongside Plausible if your priority is
    - emphasis: "\"install it and stop thinking about analytics infrastructure.\""
    - text: The tradeoff is that privacy-first simplicity means fewer of the elaborate segmentation and user-journey capabilities associated with GA4.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: 3. Umami — best for developers/self-hosting.
    - text: Umami is open source and can be self-hosted, giving you control over where the analytics data lives. It supports custom events, funnels, retention, UTM tracking, goals and APIs while remaining cookieless/privacy-focused.
    - link "Umami Docs":
      - /url: https://docs.umami.is/docs/about?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Umami Docs
    - strong: "Choose it if:"
    - text: your SaaS has engineering capacity and you value data ownership more than having a completely managed service.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: 4. Matomo — best when you need GA-like depth.
    - text: "Matomo is the heavyweight choice here: it offers much more configurability and control than Plausible/Fathom. Its privacy tooling lets you configure anonymization, cookies, consent and data retention."
    - link "Analytics Platform - Matomo":
      - /url: https://matomo.org/guide/manage-matomo/privacy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Analytics Platform - Matomo
    - text: "The catch is important:"
    - strong: Matomo isn't automatically cookieless
    - text: —its standard JavaScript tracking uses first-party cookies, although it can be configured differently.
    - link "Analytics Platform - Matomo":
      - /url: https://matomo.org/faq/general/faq_146/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Analytics Platform - Matomo
    - strong: "Choose it if:"
    - text: you need sophisticated analytics and are willing to accept more configuration/maintenance.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: 5. Simple Analytics — best if you want "just the useful numbers."
    - text: It deliberately avoids cookies, visitor IDs, personal data and cross-session tracking, with EU hosting.
    - link "Simple Analytics +1":
      - /url: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/security?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Simple Analytics
      - generic: "+1"
    - text: That makes it particularly attractive if privacy/compliance simplicity is more important than behavioral depth.
    - strong: "Choose it if:"
    - text: you mainly care about aggregate traffic, referrals, campaigns and conversions rather than reconstructing individual customer journeys.
  - heading "What I'd shortlist for a SaaS specifically" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - strong: Plausible + Umami + Matomo
    - text: "would be my first three to actually trial:"
  - list:
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Plausible
      - text: → easiest all-around replacement.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Umami
      - text: → strongest option if you want to own/self-host the data.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Matomo
      - text: → strongest if you need significantly more analytical depth.
  - paragraph:
    - text: "One important caveat:"
    - strong: website analytics ≠ product analytics
    - text: . If your real requirement is
    - emphasis: "\"Which features do logged-in customers use? Where do they drop out of onboarding? What are retention cohorts?\""
    - text: ", I'd also evaluate a privacy-conscious product-analytics platform rather than assuming a GA replacement is sufficient."
  - paragraph:
    - text: For a small SaaS whose priority is
    - strong: privacy + low maintenance + useful marketing analytics
    - text: ", though,"
    - strong: Plausible would be my default pick
    - text: .
    - link "Plausible Analytics":
      - /url: https://plausible.io/privacy-focused-web-analytics?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Plausible Analytics
